title: Ayush systems and the offices that hold them

blocks.html: Checked against the sources as they stood on 2026-10-16.

blocks.label: Definition
blocks.html:
Ayush is the Ministry of Ayush’s name for a group of systems of health care: Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy. The Union government has a Ministry of Ayush, to which the Allocation of Business Rules give the formulation of policy for these systems.

The National Health Policy 2017 (NHP) lists pluralism among its principles: patients who so choose and when appropriate would have access to Ayush care providers. Under the National Ayush Mission (NAM), Ayush facilities are co-located at primary health centres, community health centres and district hospitals.

For a question about what an Ayush system offers a patient, the owner is a qualified Ayush practitioner. For a State’s arrangements, it is the State’s Ayush directorate.

blocks.label: In plain terms
blocks.html:
You now have three tools. The five signals tell you when a question has left what you can assess. The question you would ask, in five parts, lets you send it to its owner. The five checks let you judge the reply. This section is the first field that sits inside India’s own public health system. It starts with one word: Ayush — the Ministry of Ayush’s name for Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy. The Ministry’s annual report for 2024-25 says the Ministry “has mandate to develop Ayush systems”.

The Union’s Allocation of Business Rules give the Ministry of Ayush the “Formulation of policy” for these systems. Book 5, Policy process, framing and advocacy craft, showed you how to read those rules, so they are not taught again here.

Two statutory commissions — bodies a statute sets up — regulate Ayush education: the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH).

So the field has its own standard references, its own regulators and its own practitioners, and you do not know them.

The report says the Government “has adopted a strategy of” co-location — an Ayush facility placed inside a primary health centre (PHC), community health centre (CHC) or district hospital. Patients then choose in one place. It does not say how far co-location has reached.

A second kind of Ayush place is the Ayush Health and Wellness Centre, now called Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush), or AAM (Ayush) for short: an Ayush dispensary or sub health centre upgraded, in the report’s words, “to provide comprehensive primary healthcare at grass roots level with focus on Ayush systems of medicine”. In the Ministry’s report for January to December 2024, the States and Union Territories reported 12,251 of them “progressively functional”. That is a count they reported, for that year, and it says nothing about what any one centre offers.

Now the State. The Chhattisgarh Directorate of Ayush describes itself, on its admissions-counselling website, as “a Government body under department of Medical Education (AYUSH) in Chhattisgarh Government”. The page says the directorate administers “2 Government Ayurveda Medical Colleges and 9 Private AYUSH Colleges”. It calls the directorate’s “primary responsibility” making resources “available to run the Government Colleges/Hospitals”.

That page is about colleges and their hospitals. It does not say who runs Ayush dispensaries or Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Ayush) in the State, and the directorate’s own website could not be opened for this book.

Add this row to your picture of who owns what.

Field Owner Where to look
Ayush systems a qualified Ayush practitioner; for the State’s arrangements, the State’s Ayush directorate the Ayush doctor at a PHC, CHC or district hospital where Ayush is co-located; the hospital of a government Ayush college (in Chhattisgarh, the Directorate of Ayush says it equips and staffs these)

blocks.label: Illustration 1
blocks.html:
Start with a question you cannot answer, and see where the answer would come from.

Open the Ministry of Ayush’s Annual Report 2024-25 (https://ayush.gov.in/assets/pdf/annualReport/Annual-Report24-25_English.pdf). Go to chapter 3, on the organizational set-up of central Ayush systems. Search for “Pharmacopoeia Commission”. Read what the Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy does. The report says it is working for development of “Pharmacopoeias and Formularies”, and that it acts as “Central Drug Testing cum Appellate Laboratory for Indian systems of Medicine & Homoeopathy”.

A pharmacopoeia is a standards book that says what a medicine must contain and how it is tested; a formulary lists the approved preparations and their recipes. Now ask yourself one question. Do you know which pharmacopoeia or formulary is the standard reference for a given Ayurvedic preparation, or how its contents are tested? You do not. That is the signal you met as Unknown standard, and it fires before you have read a single claim about any remedy.

Next, find who can answer. Open the National Health Policy 2017 (https://nhsrcindia.org/sites/default/files/2021-07/National%20Health%20Policy%202017%20%28English%29%20.pdf) and search for “Pluralism”. Its principle gives patients “who so choose and when appropriate” access to Ayush care providers. Then go back to the annual report, to chapter 7, and search for “Expanding Choices”. The report says Ayush facilities are placed at primary health centres, community health centres and district hospitals, and that the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare supports “Ayush doctors” there. So the person who can answer “what does this system offer, and what is in this product, by its own standards” may be in the next building.

Last, name the kind of answer. It is an answer from inside that system, made on that system’s own references. You get it by asking. You cannot produce it.

blocks.label: Where this picture breaks
blocks.html:
The report and the policy describe offices and a principle, not results. Nothing here says whether any Ayush remedy works or is safe for a given patient, and this book makes no such claim in either direction. The policy says “when appropriate” without saying when. That judgement belongs to the practitioner and the patient, and you check the reply.

The office descriptions are the Ministry’s own, as of its report for 2024. The State page describes colleges and hospitals only.

blocks.label: Illustration 2
blocks.html:
A made-up exchange: the OPD of an urban primary health centre. A woman of 52 who teaches at a government school comes for her diabetes tablets. She has obesity. She takes a packet from her bag.

“My neighbour gave me this weight-loss powder. The shop said it is Ayurvedic. Can I take it with my sugar tablets? I want to start tomorrow.”

Start with what is yours, and do it at once. Weigh her and read her diabetes record, as you would at any visit. Check that she is taking the tablets the centre prescribes. Copy the powder’s name and the contents its pack lists into her card. All of this is yours to do.

Now the signal. About to act fires first, because she will start tomorrow on what you say. Behind it sit No test, because you cannot say what result would show “it is fine with your tablets” wrong, and Unknown standard, which the Pharmacopoeia Commission’s standards books raised above. The fifth signal turns the other two from a private doubt into a duty to stop.

Suppose the centre has an Ayush unit co-located with it, as the Ministry’s strategy describes. You say the public sentence, then the owner, the next step, and what she keeps doing meanwhile: “That is outside what I can assess, and here is who can. There is an Ayush doctor at our centre, and I will send the doctor your question today. Bring the packet next time. Until the reply comes, keep taking your sugar tablets as before, and keep the powder in its packet: we change nothing until we have the answer.”

The curriculum this book follows gives the question in these words. Write it in five parts.

Part Your question
Decision At her next visit, in two weeks: whether to advise her to go on waiting, or to start with a plan for watching her. She is waiting; so is the centre’s doctor who prescribes her tablets.
Context Woman of 52 with obesity, on diabetes tablets from an urban primary health centre (names and doses attached). She wants to start a powder sold as Ayurvedic for weight loss; its name and the contents printed on its pack are attached. She asked us; she has not started it.
Question “what does this system offer this patient for weight, on what evidence, and what does it interact with in the treatment they already have?”
Form For each of the three parts: your answer, or “not known”. How sure you are, and on what: a reference I can look up, or your own experience, said as such. I cannot judge the method of your system; I can check that the answer is about this patient and this powder.
Deadline Before her next visit, in two weeks. If it comes later, she may already have started on her neighbour’s advice alone.

The question goes to the Ayush doctor at the co-located facility. If there is none, it goes to a teacher at the hospital of a government Ayush college.

Add the row to your contact list now; a later section shows how to keep it.

Field Owner Name and institution How you know them Last question asked Asked on Checked on
Ayush systems a qualified Ayush practitioner; for the State’s arrangements, the State’s Ayush directorate (yours to fill) what this system offers a patient for weight, on what evidence, and what it interacts with

blocks.label: Where this picture breaks
blocks.html:
Routing is the wrong move when the question is yours after all: whether she should keep taking her diabetes tablets, her weight, her blood sugar record. Those stay with you, and you answer them in the same visit.

It is also not routing if you send the question and stop listening. The reply still gets the five checks. And if the patient has already started the powder and is unwell, this is not a question to post and wait on. She is your patient today.

points.html: The error is to treat Ayush as something outside government that you can wave away. It has its own Union ministry. Route an Ayush question to that system’s owner, as you would any other field’s.

Do not tell a patient “it is herbal, so it is safe with your tablets”. Do not tell her “there is no evidence it works” either. Say what you can do today, and send the three-part question to an Ayush practitioner.
Copy the product’s name and listed contents into her card. Ask her to bring the pack, and send the question before her next visit.

The State directorate’s page this book holds describes colleges and their hospitals only. It does not say which office runs Ayush dispensaries or Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Ayush). Do not fill the gap with a guess.

You can judge the reply with the five checks. If it fails, ask back. If a reply conflicts with another, ask a second Ayush practitioner. If two practitioners still disagree, the field is not settled on this question: say so in those words, decide with the patient what to do meanwhile, and do not pick the view you prefer.

blocks.label: Common misreading
blocks.html: Reading the National Health Policy’s pluralism principle as the government saying Ayush remedies work for weight. The principle gives patients “who so choose and when appropriate” access to Ayush care providers. It says nothing about any remedy’s effect, and it does not say when access is appropriate.

blocks.prompt: From memory: who owns a question about what an Ayush system offers a patient for weight? Name one place in the public health system where you can find that person. Then say what the held page about Chhattisgarh’s Directorate of Ayush says the directorate is responsible for. Say also what the page does not say.
blocks.answer: A qualified Ayush practitioner. You can find one as the Ayush doctor at a primary health centre, community health centre or district hospital where Ayush is co-located under the National Ayush Mission. Another place is the hospital of a government Ayush college. The directorate’s admissions page says its primary responsibility is making infrastructure, equipment, drugs and staff available to run the government colleges and hospitals. It says the directorate administers 2 government Ayurveda colleges and 9 private Ayush colleges. It does not say who runs Ayush dispensaries or Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Ayush) in the State.

blocks.prompt: A made-up request: the medical officer of your urban primary health centre has a question. Should patients with obesity and knee pain be referred to the yoga sessions at a nearby Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush)? She will decide at next month’s staff meeting. Write the question you would ask, in the five parts, and say to whom it goes.
blocks.answer:
Part Your question
Decision Whether the centre refers its patients with obesity and knee pain to the yoga sessions; the medical officer decides at next month’s staff meeting.
Context Adults with obesity and knee pain seen at an urban primary health centre; the sessions run at a nearby AAM (Ayush); what the centre already knows about the patients (their ages, other conditions) is attached.
Question Which parts of these sessions are suitable for adults with obesity and knee pain, which should they avoid, on what evidence, and what should make them stop and see us?
Form A short list (suitable / avoid / stop signs), how sure you are and on what, and a reference I can look up. I cannot judge yoga’s method myself.
Deadline One week before the staff meeting; if later, the decision is made without your answer.

It goes to the qualified practitioner who runs or supervises the sessions, because Yoga is one of the Ayush systems. The AAM (Ayush) will tell you who that is.

Notice what stays yours: which of the centre’s patients have knee pain, and how you will know whether those referred came back better or worse.

blocks.prompt: A made-up line from a colleague in the OPD, to the patient of this section: “It’s herbal, so it won’t interact with your diabetes tablets. Try it for a month.” Name the signal that should have stopped your colleague, say why the line is improvising, and rewrite it.
blocks.answer:
About to act fires first: she will start on his word. Behind it is No test. He cannot say what result would show “it won’t interact” wrong, and “herbal” is a Loose word doing the work of an argument. The line is improvising because it is confident and he cannot check it. It also says something about the product’s effect. Neither he nor you can assess that.

Rewrite: “That is outside what I can assess, and here is who can: the Ayush doctor at our centre. Keep taking your tablets as before. I’ll ask the Ayush doctor at the centre and tell you at your next visit; bring the packet.”

Notice what the rewrite does not say: that the powder is safe, unsafe, useful or useless.
